$comment: CROSS-LANGUAGE CONTRACT FIXTURE — one shared definition of where a Vega-Lite spec's rows live. Consumed by web/app/components/shared/__tests__/VegaChart.dom.test.tsx (specDataRows) and, once PR #986 lands, by the pytest for ChartSpec.row_count(). Both implementations must return the same rowCount for every case here. This file exists because the two sides drifted: the client walked containers while the server read the root only, and NEITHER resolved altair's default named-dataset shape — so one spec produced three different answers (client-envelope: empty, client-bare: drawn, server: 'No data.'). Add a case here BEFORE fixing a row-extraction bug on either side, so the fix lands on both.
$definition: Rows live at: (1) the root's `data`, (2) any nested container's `data` — layer / concat / hconcat / vconcat / spec, (3) a named reference `data: {name}` resolved against the ROOT `datasets` map. Inline `values` wins over a named reference on the same node. The first container that yields rows wins; containers are searched in the order listed above. A row is a JSON object; non-object array elements are not rows.

cases.name: layered — data hangs off a layer, not the root (ITS / DiD / K-M shape)
altair default — named dataset reference, rows hoisted to `datasets`
cases.$note: What altair.to_dict() emits by DEFAULT: its data transformer names and hoists the rows rather than inlining them. Phase 1's DS sandbox writes altair specs, so this is the ordinary shape. A reader that only understands inline `values` reports these charts as having no data.

named reference resolving to an empty dataset
named reference with no matching dataset
inline values win over a named reference on the same node
generator — rows not visible from here
non-object array elements are not rows
first container that yields rows wins
